hot.title: Attention Residuals
hot.summary: The Kimi Team introduced Attention Residuals (AttnRes) for deep neural networks, which replaces standard residual connections' fixed additive accumulation with learned, content-dependent softmax attention over preceding layer outputs. The scalable Block AttnRes variant mitigated hidden-state growth and dilution, achieving lower validation loss and outperforming baselines by up to 7.5 points on multi-step reasoning tasks like GPQA-Diamond.

hot.title: Mamba-3: Improved Sequence Modeling using State Space Principles
hot.summary: Mamba-3 introduces a State Space Model architecture featuring exponential-trapezoidal discretization, complex-valued states, and a multi-input, multi-output formulation to improve sequence modeling. It demonstrates superior language modeling quality and enhanced inference efficiency compared to prior linear models like Mamba-2 and GDN, achieving a 1.8 percentage point accuracy gain over GDN at the 1.5B scale and lower decode latency.

hot.title: AI Can Learn Scientific Taste
hot.summary: Researchers from Fudan University and collaborators developed OpenMOSS, an AI framework designed to acquire "scientific taste" for judging and generating high-impact research ideas. Their Reinforcement Learning from Community Feedback (RLCF) approach, which uses citation data as supervision, yielded a Scientific Judge model that surpassed leading proprietary LLMs in predicting paper impact and a Scientific Thinker model capable of generating research ideas with superior win rates against strong LLMs.

hot.title: Mixture-of-Depths Attention
hot.summary: Researchers from Huazhong University of Science & Technology and ByteDance Seed developed Mixture-of-Depths Attention (MoDA), an architectural component that allows deep layers in large language models to dynamically retrieve information from all preceding layers. MoDA consistently improved perplexity and downstream task performance by 1.17-2.11 percentage points across model scales from 700M to 1.5B parameters, while achieving near FlashAttention-2 efficiency with a hardware-aware implementation.

hot.title: V-JEPA 2.1: Unlocking Dense Features in Video Self-Supervised Learning
hot.summary: V-JEPA 2.1, developed by FAIR at Meta, introduces innovations in self-supervised video learning to produce high-quality dense visual features while maintaining robust global understanding. The model achieves new state-of-the-art performance across diverse benchmarks, including a 35% relative improvement in short-term object interaction anticipation and significantly improved depth estimation with an RMSE of 0.307 on NYUv2.

hot.title: Why AI systems don't learn and what to do about it: Lessons on autonomous learning from cognitive science
hot.summary: Researchers from FAIR at META, NYU, and UC Berkeley propose a conceptual architecture for autonomous learning systems in AI, drawing inspiration from cognitive science. Their framework integrates learning from observation (System A), learning from action (System B), and a meta-control system (System M) to enable continuous, self-improving AI capable of adapting to dynamic, real-world environments without constant human intervention. They also outline an Evolutionary-Developmental (Evo/Devo) framework for bootstrapping this interdependent architecture.

hot.title: Online Experiential Learning for Language Models
hot.summary: Microsoft Research introduced an Online Experiential Learning (OEL) framework that allows large language models to continuously refine their capabilities directly from real-world textual interactions, circumventing the need for explicit reward signals or human annotations. This iterative approach to extracting and consolidating experiential knowledge into model parameters yielded progressive gains in task accuracy, reduced response lengths by up to 30% in experiments, and maintained out-of-distribution performance.

hot.title: Delightful Policy Gradient
hot.summary: Google DeepMind's Delightful Policy Gradient (DG) reframes policy learning by re-weighting gradient terms based on both action advantage and surprisal, differentiating between rare successful actions and rare detrimental ones. This approach improves learning dynamics, leading to more efficient convergence and better performance across various reinforcement learning tasks, especially in complex settings.

hot.title: Demystifing Video Reasoning
hot.summary: This research investigates how diffusion-based video models perform reasoning, proposing and empirically validating a "Chain-of-Steps" mechanism where logical problem-solving unfolds across denoising steps, rather than sequentially across video frames. Researchers demonstrated that models explore multiple candidate solutions and self-correct during denoising, and introduced a training-free ensemble method that improved reasoning performance by 2% on the VBVR-Bench benchmark.

hot.title: MiroThinker-1.7 & H1: Towards Heavy-Duty Research Agents via Verification
hot.summary: MiroThinker-1.7 and MiroThinker-H1 are AI agents designed to enhance long-horizon reasoning by focusing on effective interaction and explicit verification. MiroThinker-H1, employing a "heavy-duty" reasoning mode with local and global verifiers, achieved an 88.5 score on GAIA and demonstrated higher report quality in deep research queries, while MiroThinker-1.7-mini improved performance by 16.7% with 43.0% fewer interaction rounds on agentic benchmarks.

hot.title: The Finetuner's Fallacy: When to Pretrain with Your Finetuning Data
hot.summary: Specialized Pretraining (SPT), an approach that integrates domain-specific data into the initial pretraining of large language models, consistently improves domain test loss by 0.8% to 2.0% and reduces required compute by up to 1.75x compared to conventional finetuning-only strategies.

hot.title: OpenSeeker: Democratizing Frontier Search Agents by Fully Open-Sourcing Training Data
hot.summary: An academic team at Shanghai Jiao Tong University released OpenSeeker, a fully open-source search agent complete with its training data and synthesis pipeline, demonstrating competitive web search performance against industrial models using a streamlined supervised fine-tuning approach. The project aims to democratize advanced search agent development by providing transparent, high-quality resources.

hot.title: Autonomous Agents Coordinating Distributed Discovery Through Emergent Artifact Exchange
hot.summary: A framework named SCIENCECLAW + INFINITE enables autonomous AI agents to conduct decentralized scientific investigations, fostering emergent collaboration through structured artifact exchange and tool chaining. The system demonstrated its capacity for generating traceable discoveries and identifying complex insights across domains like protein design, materials science, and cross-domain analogies.

hot.title: HorizonMath: Measuring AI Progress Toward Mathematical Discovery with Automatic Verification
hot.summary: HorizonMath is a benchmark composed of over 100 predominantly unsolved mathematical problems, designed to measure AI progress in autonomous discovery through automated verification. Evaluations showed GPT 5.4 Pro proposed potentially novel improvements to best-known baselines for two optimization problems.

hot.title: Understanding Reasoning in LLMs through Strategic Information Allocation under Uncertainty
hot.summary: This research introduces an information-theoretic framework to explain reasoning and self-correction in Large Language Models (LLMs) by positing that "epistemic verbalization"—the externalization of internal uncertainty—helps overcome informational stagnation. Empirical findings demonstrate that this verbalization correlates with a model's underlying uncertainty, and its strategic integration is essential for effective reasoning and successful knowledge distillation.

hot.title: OpenClaw-RL: Train Any Agent Simply by Talking
hot.summary: OpenClaw-RL is a framework that systematically converts real-time next-state signals from AI agent interactions into continuous, online learning sources. The system recovers both implicit evaluative signals and explicit directive signals, enabling agents to achieve rapid personalization in conversational settings and improve performance across diverse general agent tasks like terminal, GUI, SWE, and tool-calling environments.

hot.title: WorldCam: Interactive Autoregressive 3D Gaming Worlds with Camera Pose as a Unifying Geometric Representation
hot.summary: Researchers developed WorldCam, a model for interactive 3D gaming worlds that utilizes camera pose as a unified geometric representation to enhance action control and long-term 3D consistency. It achieved lower relative pose errors, higher visual quality, and improved spatial coherence compared to existing models, while also introducing a large-scale, open-licensed gameplay dataset.

hot.title: Grounding World Simulation Models in a Real-World Metropolis
hot.summary: KAIST AI and NAVER AI Lab introduced the Seoul World Model (SWM), the first video world simulation model capable of operating within a real city rather than an imagined environment. This model generates dynamic, long-horizon urban scenarios from street-view data, demonstrating superior visual fidelity and 3D adherence on city-scale benchmarks compared to existing baselines.

hot.title: Neural Thickets: Diverse Task Experts Are Dense Around Pretrained Weights
hot.summary: MIT CSAIL researchers Yulu Gan and Phillip Isola propose that large pretrained neural networks exist in a "thicket" regime, where their weight space is dense with diverse task-specific experts accessible via simple random perturbations. Their "RandOpt" algorithm, which randomly samples and ensembles these perturbations, achieved performance competitive with or superior to established gradient-based post-training methods on various LLM and VLM tasks.

hot.title: Fast-WAM: Do World Action Models Need Test-time Future Imagination?
hot.summary: Researchers from Tsinghua University and Galaxea AI developed Fast-WAM, a World Action Model (WAM) that achieves competitive robotic task performance with significantly reduced inference latency by leveraging video co-training during learning but skipping explicit future imagination at test time. This approach attains up to 97.6% success rates on LIBERO and RoboTwin benchmarks and over 4x faster inference compared to imagine-then-execute WAMs.

likes.title: Perception Encoder: The best visual embeddings are not at the output of  the network
likes.summary: Perception Encoder introduces a family of vision models that achieve state-of-the-art performance across diverse vision and vision-language tasks, demonstrating that general, high-quality visual features can be extracted from the intermediate layers of a single, contrastively-trained network. It provides specific alignment tuning methods to make these features accessible for tasks ranging from zero-shot classification to dense spatial prediction and multimodal language understanding.

likes.title: TTRL: Test-Time Reinforcement Learning
likes.summary: TTRL is a framework enabling Large Language Models to self-improve through Reinforcement Learning on unlabeled test data, using self-generated rewards derived from majority voting. This approach substantially boosts performance on complex reasoning tasks, with one model achieving a 211% improvement on AIME 2024, by fostering a self-reinforcing learning loop.

likes.title: Inference-Time Scaling for Generalist Reward Modeling
likes.summary: DeepSeek-AI and Tsinghua University developed Self-Principled Critique Tuning (SPCT) and DeepSeek-GRM models, a pointwise generative reward modeling approach that achieves state-of-the-art performance in generalist reward benchmarks. This method demonstrates effective inference-time scalability, allowing smaller models to match or exceed the performance of much larger models by leveraging increased compute during inference, thereby improving LLM alignment.

likes.title: Does Reinforcement Learning Really Incentivize Reasoning Capacity in LLMs Beyond the Base Model?
likes.summary: Research from Tsinghua University reveals that current Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) primarily enhances the sampling efficiency of Large Language Models for already existing reasoning patterns. This optimization often narrows the models' overall reasoning capacity at higher pass@k values, contrasting with distillation, which effectively expands their problem-solving scope.

likes.title: Reasoning Models Can Be Effective Without Thinking
likes.summary: Ma et al. demonstrated that Large Language Models trained for Chain-of-Thought reasoning can achieve comparable or superior performance without generating explicit reasoning steps, utilizing a technique called 'NoThinking'. This approach significantly reduces inference latency by up to 9x and token usage by up to 5.1x, particularly when combined with parallel sampling, offering a more efficient paradigm for LLM reasoning.

likes.title: Synthetic Data Generation & Multi-Step RL for Reasoning & Tool Use
likes.summary: SWiRL is an offline multi-step reinforcement learning methodology designed to enhance Large Language Models' reasoning and tool-use capabilities. It generates and utilizes synthetic data, applying process-based filtering for step-wise optimization, which leads to substantial performance gains and strong cross-domain generalization in complex tasks.

likes.title: ReTool: Reinforcement Learning for Strategic Tool Use in LLMs
likes.summary: ReTool, developed by ByteDance Seed, introduces a reinforcement learning framework that enables Large Language Models to strategically use code interpreters for complex problem-solving. It achieved 67.0% accuracy on the AIME 2024 benchmark, significantly improving performance over text-based reasoning and demonstrating emergent self-correction capabilities in code generation.

likes.title: Hogwild! Inference: Parallel LLM Generation via Concurrent Attention
likes.summary: Researchers from Yandex, HSE University, and IST Austria developed "Hogwild! Inference," a protocol enabling multiple Large Language Models (LLMs) to generate text concurrently by sharing a dynamically updated attention Key-Value (KV) cache. This mechanism allows LLMs to self-organize and collaborate in real-time, achieving up to 3.6x speedup and improved accuracy on complex reasoning tasks.

likes.title: Challenges and Paths Towards AI for Software Engineering
likes.summary: This paper presents a strategic roadmap for the field of AI in software engineering, providing a comprehensive taxonomy of software development tasks and identifying nine key bottlenecks that impede current AI capabilities. It proposes a targeted set of research directions focused on data collection, training, and inference-time approaches to advance automated software development.

likes.title: DAPO: An Open-Source LLM Reinforcement Learning System at Scale
likes.summary: Researchers from ByteDance Seed, Tsinghua University, and The University of Hong Kong developed DAPO, an open-source reinforcement learning system for large language models. The system achieved 50 points on the AIME 2024 dataset with a Qwen2.5-32B model, surpassing the prior 47-point score of DeepSeek-R1-Zero-Qwen-32B while requiring 50% fewer training steps.

likes.title: Proof or Bluff? Evaluating LLMs on 2025 USA Math Olympiad
likes.summary: Researchers from ETH Zurich and INSAIT conducted the first evaluation of large language models on generating rigorous natural language proofs for problems from the 2025 USA Mathematical Olympiad. The study found that most state-of-the-art models scored below 5% of the maximum points, with the highest-performing model, GEMINI-2.5-PRO, achieving only 24.4%, demonstrating fundamental shortcomings in advanced mathematical reasoning capabilities.

likes.title: DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLMs via Reinforcement Learning
likes.summary: DeepSeek-AI developed DeepSeek-R1, an LLM demonstrating that sophisticated reasoning capabilities can emerge through pure outcome-based reinforcement learning without reliance on human-annotated reasoning trajectories. The model achieved an AIME 2024 pass@1 accuracy of 77.9% with R1-Zero, and the multi-stage DeepSeek-R1 surpassed state-of-the-art models on numerous math, coding, and STEM benchmarks while exhibiting emergent self-reflection and dynamic strategy adaptation.

likes.title: ReSearch: Learning to Reason with Search for LLMs via Reinforcement Learning
likes.summary: The ReSearch framework enables Large Language Models to integrate multi-step reasoning with external search, learning interactively via reinforcement learning without supervised intermediate steps. It yields substantial performance gains on complex multi-hop question answering benchmarks and reveals emergent self-correction capabilities.

likes.title: Insights into DeepSeek-V3: Scaling Challenges and Reflections on Hardware for AI Architectures
likes.summary: DeepSeek-V3 showcases how a hardware-software co-design strategy can achieve state-of-the-art large language model performance using a comparatively modest cluster of 2,048 NVIDIA H800 GPUs. The paper highlights innovations like Multi-head Latent Attention, DeepSeekMoE, FP8 mixed-precision training, and a Multi-Plane Fat-Tree network, which collectively reduce memory consumption, lower training costs, and accelerate inference.

likes.title: One-Minute Video Generation with Test-Time Training
likes.summary: Researchers from NVIDIA and leading universities introduce Test-Time Training (TTT) layers within pre-trained Diffusion Transformers to generate one-minute-long videos from text storyboards, enabling coherent multi-scene narratives while addressing the computational limitations of traditional self-attention mechanisms for long sequences.

likes.title: Sequential Task Assignment and Resource Allocation in V2X-Enabled Mobile  Edge Computing
likes.summary: A multi-tier task offloading mechanism for V2X-enabled Mobile Edge Computing efficiently processes sequential subtasks from vehicular applications by first leveraging proximate vehicle resources and then RSU-based MEC. The system minimizes energy consumption while meeting stringent delay requirements through joint optimization of offloading decisions, communication, and computation resource allocation, demonstrating superior performance over various baselines.

likes.title: How new data permeates LLM knowledge and how to dilute it
likes.summary: Research from Google DeepMind reveals how new knowledge permeates through large language models, demonstrating that surprising information (measured by token probability) leads to broader changes across model behavior, while introducing "stepping-stone" text augmentation and "ignore-k" update pruning techniques that reduce undesirable priming effects by 50-95%.

likes.title: Titans: Learning to Memorize at Test Time
likes.summary: Titans introduces a new neural memory module that learns to memorize information at test time and effectively combines with attention mechanisms for better long-term sequence modeling

likes.title: PHYBench: Holistic Evaluation of Physical Perception and Reasoning in  Large Language Models
likes.summary: PHYBench, a new benchmark developed by the School of Physics at Peking University, rigorously evaluates large language models' physical perception and reasoning using 500 original, human-curated physics problems. Evaluations revealed a substantial performance gap between LLMs and human experts, with the best LLM achieving 36.9% accuracy compared to the human baseline of 61.9%.

likes.title: Transformers without Normalization
likes.summary: This research introduces Dynamic Tanh (DyT), a simple element-wise function designed as a drop-in replacement for normalization layers in Transformers. Models equipped with DyT achieve performance comparable to or exceeding their normalized counterparts across a wide range of tasks including computer vision, large language models, and speech processing, often without requiring extensive hyperparameter tuning.
